description: DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village features research on automotive security, embedded systems, wireless protocols, and real-world vehicle hacking techniques including GPS spoofing, ECU firmware, keyless entry systems, and infotainment platforms.

talks.title: Victor Murray - Legal Over the Air Spoofing of GNSS and its Effects - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser: Many systems depend on accurate location information from Global Navigation System Satellites (GNSS) for normal operation.
talks.summary: Many systems depend on accurate location information from Global Navigation System Satellites (GNSS) for normal operation. Public GNSS lacks integrity mechanisms and is vulnerable to spoofing. U.S. Federal law does not allow over-the-air spoofing of GNSS or other signals, which makes assessment of vulnerabilities difficult outside of an enclosed laboratory environment. This research proved the usefulness of a Mobile GNSS Spoofing System that enables legal, real-world evaluation of GNSS vulnerabilities. The mobile spoofing system was used to evaluate vulnerabilities in an Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV). The UGV GNSS was exploited using several different attacks including forced lane switching, driving off the road, and stopping the vehicle.

talks.title: Rotem Bar - Hacking into Automotive Clouds - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser: In this talk Rotem will share my experience about how he hacked different automotive clouds, techniques he used and goals pursued after connecting.
talks.summary: In this talk Rotem will share my experience about how he hacked different automotive clouds, techniques he used and goals pursued after connecting.

talks.title: Neiko Rivera - Infotainment Hacking - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser: Showing the inside of QNX and Android with a high overview of each system and there unique attributes.
talks.summary:
Showing the inside of QNX and Android with a high overview of each system and there unique attributes. Finding common misconfigurations in Android systems, while also showing people how to extract and begin the process to reverse engineer (but no in depth reversing of apks).

Hardware hacking on systems to gain escalated privileges to obtain initial foothold on device and begin reverse engineering from there!

talks.title: Lennert Wouters - Passive Keyless Entry and Start Systems - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser: Our research revealed several weaknesses in the Tesla Model S passive keyless entry and start system.
talks.summary: Our research revealed several weaknesses in the Tesla Model S passive keyless entry and start system. The talk will be a comprehensive overview of how we reverse engineered the key fob, the issues we found and an efficient proof of concept attack. The proof of concept attack exploits the use of an inadequate cipher and allows us to clone a Tesla Model S key fob in a matter of seconds using commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Information from the FCC database suggests that the same attack could affect vehicles produced by McLaren, Karma and Triumph Motorcycles as they all use a passive keyless entry and start system designed by Pektron. I will share our experience with responsibly disclosing our findings with all the manufacturers.

talks.title: Elijah Roberts - Tell Me Lies Automotive LIDAR and Low Tech - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser:
What will it mean if LIDAR becomes ubiquitous in autonomous vehicles? 

Join us for an exploration of a LIDAR’s operation, network attack surface, and the development of low-tech countermeasures that render solid objects
talks.summary: What will it mean if LIDAR becomes ubiquitous in autonomous vehicles?

talks.title: Greg Hogan - Reverse Engineering and Flashing ECU Firmware Updates - DEF CON 27 Car Hacking Village
talks.teaser: Many ECUs do not support reading firmware over CAN, but since automotive manufacturers make mistakes and need to fix firmware bugs, they release firmware updates and support writing firmware over CAN.
talks.summary: Many ECUs do not support reading firmware over CAN, but since automotive manufacturers make mistakes and need to fix firmware bugs, they release firmware updates and support writing firmware over CAN. This will be a deep dive into how you can obtain these firmware updates, decrypt them, (modify if you like) and flash a firmware update file for Honda ECUs. The ECU tools provided by automotive manufacturers are from the stone age, so let’s use a modern web browser to flash an ECU!
